In the notebook's scenario that is about `{python} CanaryExcessFailures.excess_canary_str` at the canary fraction and about `{python} CanaryExcessFailures.excess_full_str` at full allocation. The fraction enters only through the label delay; its main effect on a measured regression is the calendar time needed to collect the samples.

Harms the monitor does not measure behave differently. They accrue for every admitted candidate task until some other mechanism detects them, so their rate scales with $\rho$, and this canary exposes candidate tasks at `{python} SizingCanaryTrafficCircuitBreaker.fraction_pct_str` of the full-allocation rate. The test's sample size fixes the harm from a measured regression; the canary's size limits the harms the test does not measure. A production release of a foundation model shows what the second kind of harm looks like when it escapes.

::: {#ws-vol3-evaluation-gpt4o-sycophancy-2025 .callout-war-story title="The GPT-4o sycophancy rollback (2025)"}

**Context**: In late April 2025, OpenAI rolled out an update to the GPT-4o model behind ChatGPT, adjusting its default personality [@openai2025sycophancy].

**Mechanism**: By OpenAI's account, the update focused too much on short-term user feedback and did not account for how users' interactions evolve over time. The model skewed toward responses that were overly supportive but disingenuous. OpenAI's follow-up analysis reports that changes including an added reward signal from user thumbs-up and thumbs-down feedback weakened the influence of the primary reward that had held sycophancy in check, and that the offline evaluations and the A/B test of the update both looked good before launch [@openai2025expanding].

**Impact**: The update reached ChatGPT users before the behavior was recognized, and OpenAI rolled it back, returning users to an earlier version with more balanced behavior.

**Fix**: OpenAI committed to refining training techniques and system prompts to steer the model away from sycophancy, adding guardrails for honesty and transparency, expanding predeployment testing with direct user feedback, and expanding its evaluations to catch behavioral issues beyond sycophancy.

**Systems lesson**: A release gate passes exactly the criteria it declares. A regression in a property that no criterion measures clears every term of the gate, and no sequential monitor can stop it because none is watching it. The durable responses are a new criterion for the next release and an admission hold on the regressed configuration.

:::

The sycophancy regression is that unmeasured harm at full scale. Detection came from outside the declared criteria, and the effective response was an admission stop on the regressed configuration followed by settlement of what it had already done.

### Stop admission without erasing outstanding work

A hard operational tripwire does not wait for statistical evidence. A verified forbidden dispatch, an exhausted release allowance, or too much unresolved candidate work stops further admission under the declared policy. A task-count cap bounds effects only when each task's effects are also bounded at enforcing endpoints (@sec-vol3-controlplane-accounting); a routing percentage alone supplies neither bound.

Rollback changes which configuration may receive new work. It does not retract transmitted requests, restore changed objects, or make a baseline worker eligible to continue a candidate trajectory without the ownership and compatibility checks of @sec-vol3-persistence-migration. Outstanding candidate operations keep their original identities, and the recovery policy of @sec-vol3-failure-recovery governs their effects, cleanup, and residual owners. Detection, confirmed admission stop, and effect settlement are distinct intervals, and effects that cannot be undone or remain unknown at the cutoff stay out of any average that implies every case was restored.

### Count accepted work over the observed interval

Release reporting keeps a fraction of tasks, a rate of completion, and the resources spent producing them distinct. The accepted task is the unit that trajectory goodput (principle \ref{pri-vol3-trajectory-goodput}) charges all initiated work against. For a declared admitted cohort of size $N$, let $N_{\text{accepted}}$ count tasks meeting the complete acceptance contract by the observation cutoff, so $q_{\text{observed}}=N_{\text{accepted}}/N$, with pending and unknown cases reported as separate counts rather than scored as failures.

For an observation interval $[t_a,t_b)$, let $N_{\text{accepted}}[t_a,t_b)$ count acceptance events in that interval under the declared measurement policy. **Verified throughput**\index{Verified throughput!definition} is

$$\Theta = \frac{N_{\text{accepted}}[t_a,t_b)}{t_b-t_a}.$$

The denominator is elapsed observation time, not the sum of overlapping task durations, and the report states startup and drain treatment, concurrency, and arrival policy. A small canary can be arrival-limited, so its raw throughput is not comparable with a fully loaded baseline's capacity. @Tbl-vol3-sre-metrics keeps companion measurements tied to their denominators.

| Measurement                | Denominator or boundary                                                                                   | Interpretation to preserve                                                                    |
|:---------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Observed accepted fraction | All tasks in the declared admitted cohort                                                                 | Report failed, pending, and unknown cases separately                                          |
| Verified throughput        | Elapsed observation interval                                                                              | Match workload and capacity before comparing rates                                            |
| Cost per accepted task     | Accepted count, with all included cohort costs in the numerator                                           | Include failed work and report unsettled liability; undefined when none are accepted          |
| Intervention burden        | Events per task, or tasks with an intervention divided by all tasks                                       | Event counts can exceed one per task; routine required approval is not automatically a defect |
| Latency and settlement     | Named start/end events and observation cutoff                                                             | Report unresolved cases; an empirical percentile is not a hard per-task deadline              |
| Behavioral change          | Comparable input mix and declared action-counting policy; $D_{\mathrm{JS}}$ from @eq-vol3-eval-tool-drift | A different tool distribution may reflect improvement, regression, or changed demand          |

: **Release measurements and their scope**: Operational signals retain their units and populations. Zero observed violations does not establish zero future risk, and a denied proposal is distinct from an escaped effect. {#tbl-vol3-sre-metrics}

The paired comparison, diagnostic experiment, and sequential monitor answer different questions and cannot substitute for one another. A coherent release record brings them together with their fixtures, limits, and residual obligations so that the resulting decision can be inspected.

## An Evidence-Backed Evaluation Decision {#sec-vol3-evaluation-synthesis}

`candidate_v2` accepts more tasks than `baseline_v1` in the paired sample, and a separate diagnostic experiment suggests a useful interface repair. Neither result, by itself, clears the release rule. We can now assemble the evidence to see what is ready, what remains unresolved, and which next experiment is justified.

### Assemble the decision record {#sec-vol3-evaluation-synthesis-architecture}

@Tbl-vol3-controlplane-layers brings together the chapter's hypothetical trial, paired comparison, and diagnostic experiment, preserving each experiment's identity so that a useful finding cannot silently become evidence for a different claim. The record references protected artifacts rather than copying them and marks unavailable material explicitly.

| Evidence record field           | Entry or required reference                                                                                                                   | Decision consequence                                                                                                                                                                           |
|:--------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Task, fixture, and criteria     | `pool_repair_01`, `pool_fixture_v1`, `repair_accept_v1`; record permitted effects, required checks, budgets, and residual-duty conditions     | The verdict concerns this declared task contract, not unrestricted correctness.                                                                                                                |
| Trial and artifact identity     | The worked trial, configuration `candidate_v2`, artifact `ws_r19`; preserve grader and check versions                                         | Do not confuse a trial, system configuration, source artifact, or historical operation.                                                                                                        |
| Individual trial verdict        | Targeted check passed; required regression evidence remains pending in the opening worksheet                                                  | Do not accept the trial merely because one check passed. Preserve other established failures or unknowns independently.                                                                        |
| Paired comparison               | The complete task-pair record and candidate-minus-baseline interval from @sec-vol3-evaluation-rigor, with its prespecified degradation margin | The worked comparison does not establish noninferiority; favorable marginal counts do not override that result.                                                                                |
| Resources and unresolved duties | Account for all started generation, grading, tools, and declared finalization; retain actual charges and outstanding liability separately     | A pending final bill is not zero cost. Whether sufficient bounded evidence satisfies a criterion follows the stated contract.                                                                  |
| Capture and privacy             | Retained trace boundaries, payload availability, sampling probabilities, delayed verdicts, drops, and authorized evidence access              | Diagnostic completeness and population representativeness require evidence; redacted bytes cannot be claimed available for exact replay.                                                       |
| Diagnosis and regression        | The controlled observation-interface experiment and its fixture-specific regression tests                                                     | Support a scoped intervention hypothesis without labeling the model or interface the sole possible cause. Its repeated fixture runs are not additional independent tasks in the paired cohort. |
| Release disposition             | Retain the baseline; no live promotion of this candidate on the current evidence                                                              | Further work needs a stated question and planned evidence collection, not an automatic increase in traffic.                                                                                    |

: **An integrated evaluation record**: Each field identifies what the evidence supports and which decision it constrains. Missing or pending evidence remains visible rather than becoming an implicit pass. {#tbl-vol3-controlplane-layers}

### Check whether the evidence answers the question {#sec-vol3-evaluation-synthesis-readiness}

The record exposes three different next actions. The individual repair needs its regression and accounting results, the interface change needs tests beyond its saved diagnostic fixture, and the release question needs evidence sufficient for its prespecified margin. One more detailed trace answers none of the three.

Collecting more evidence differs from changing the question. Removing difficult tasks, excluding pending results, enlarging the budget, or changing the selector can raise a reported rate while changing its meaning. A legitimate revision records a new protocol or configuration and evaluates it afresh; it does not retrospectively redefine the original experiment as successful.

### Apply the declared decision rule {#sec-vol3-evaluation-synthesis-math}

The worked paired interval extends below the allowed degradation, so the evidence establishes neither noninferiority nor superiority. That bounds what this experiment supports without finding the candidate worse, and notebook \ref{nbk-vol3-evaluation-wilson-superiority} prices the remedy at about `{python} PairedAcceptance.n_if_gain_holds_str` pairs if the observed gain holds. Operationally, a declared decision rule is a conjunction of criteria, each tied to its own evidence:

$$G=\mathbf{1}\!\left[L_\Delta>-\delta_{\mathrm{tol}}\right]\wedge
\mathbf{1}\!\left[\Theta_c\ge(1-\epsilon_\Theta)\,\Theta_b\right]\wedge
\mathbf{1}\!\left[\widehat T_{c,0.99}\le T_{\max}\right]\wedge
\mathbf{1}\!\left[V_c=0\right].$$ {#eq-vol3-eval-release-gate}

The first term in @eq-vol3-eval-release-gate is the paired noninferiority criterion. The second compares verified throughput $\Theta$ over matched intervals, workloads, and capacity, within a declared tolerance $\epsilon_\Theta$. The third bounds an empirical high-percentile completion time against a declared ceiling $T_{\max}$; it is an estimate over the cohort, not a per-task deadline. The fourth is different in kind. $V_c$ counts verified forbidden effects, and a single one fails the gate as a hard tripwire; zero observed violations remains an observation of this cohort. A behavioral-drift measure such as @eq-vol3-eval-tool-drift beyond its declared threshold routes the decision to review rather than failing it, because a changed tool distribution can be the intended repair. The conjunction fails when any term fails, so favorable latency, a lower bill, or a clean violation count cannot offset the unmet acceptance-rate requirement. The conjunction also passes anything outside its four terms, the lesson of war story \ref{ws-vol3-evaluation-gpt4o-sycophancy-2025}.

The decision is therefore to retain `baseline_v1` and withhold live promotion of `candidate_v2`, then resolve the trial's pending evidence and plan any further comparison before collecting its data. An automated gate enforces this policy deterministically while its statistical premises remain as uncertain as their evidence, so the report states whether each criterion passed, failed, or remains inconclusive. Several nominal confidence statements do not combine into one confidence level for the whole report, and the protocol states which hypotheses and repeated looks its error accounting covers.

::: {.callout-checkpoint title="Defend the evaluation decision"}

- [ ] **Evidence scope**: Why does the targeted pass for `ws_r19` not accept its trial while the required regression result is pending? Why is a recovered result for `ws_r18` not a replacement?
- [ ] **Comparison**: Why can a candidate have more accepted trials in the paired sample without clearing the prespecified noninferiority rule?
- [ ] **Diagnosis**: What does a successful observation-interface intervention on one fixture support, and what broader claim still needs evaluation?
- [ ] **Next step**: Using the paired-comparison notebook's planning formula, how many task pairs would you plan if you believed the true gain were half the observed one? How would you keep repeated testing or selective exclusions from changing the claimed decision rule?

:::

The useful product of evaluation is this accountable decision, naming the tested configuration, the evidence and its limits, the permitted next step, and the obligations still open.

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-vol3-evaluation-fallacies}

The strongest-looking evaluation report can still answer the wrong question. Each mistake below breaks the link between a piece of evidence and the claim drawn from it, and each has a price the chapter's own arithmetic can state.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *An agent that succeeds on `{python} PassPowK.p_hi_pct_str` of runs is a reliable agent.*

Single-run success measures one delivery, and recurring work compounds like a horizon (@sec-vol3-evaluation-pass-k). At `{python} PassPowK.p_hi_pct_str` single-run acceptance, a task that recurs `{python} PassPowK.k_str` times passes every time only `{python} PassPowK.pow_hi_str` of the time, and holding `{python} PassPowK.target_str` consistency needs a single-run rate of `{python} PassPowK.p_needed_str`. Report pass$^k$ for work that must succeed each time, and selected acceptance for work a checker can retry.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Comparing two systems by whether their separate confidence intervals overlap.*

Marginal Wilson intervals estimate individual rates, while the release question concerns their paired difference (@sec-vol3-evaluation-paired). In the worked comparison, pairing leaves about `{python} SampleSizeScale.paired_share_str` of the variance two independent arms would carry, so an unpaired analysis needs about `{python} SampleSizeScale.independent_mult_str` as many tasks for the same precision. Preserve task pairing, fix the tolerance before inspection, and decide on the lower bound of the paired interval.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *A grader that is isolated from the agent and agrees with a second judge is a correct grader.*

Isolation protects the integrity of a measurement and agreement measures consistency; neither measures correctness (@sec-vol3-evaluation-grading). Two raters who each pass `{python} KappaChance.pass_rate_str` of cases without looking at them agree on `{python} KappaChance.p_o_str` of cases with $\kappa$ of `{python} KappaChance.kappa_str`. Calibrate against independently assessed failures and report the false-acceptance rate.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Relying on uniform head sampling to keep examples of rare failures.*

Head sampling decides before the outcome is known (@sec-vol3-evaluation-budgets). At a `{python} HeadSamplingMiss.theta_str` sampling rate, a failure mode seen `{python} HeadSamplingMiss.rare_count_str` times leaves no detailed trace `{python} HeadSamplingMiss.miss_rare_str` of the time. Select on verdicts, keep a known control sample for rates, and take the failure rate from the complete accounting record.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *A small canary fraction limits the damage a regression can do.*

For a regression the monitor measures, the damage is set by the sample count needed to decide (@sec-vol3-evaluation-releases). In the worked monitor it is about `{python} CanaryExcessFailures.excess_canary_str` excess failures at a `{python} SizingCanaryTrafficCircuitBreaker.fraction_pct_str` allocation and about `{python} CanaryExcessFailures.excess_full_str` at full allocation, while the small fraction stretches the decision to `{python} SizingCanaryTrafficCircuitBreaker.label_time_str`. The fraction limits only harms the monitor does not watch, which is why hard tripwires and effect limits stay independent of it.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Treating a clean diagnostic run or a rollback as closing the incident.*

A controlled intervention supports a conclusion under its fixture (@sec-vol3-postmortem-ablation). `{python} DiagnosticCounts.revised_accepted_str` accepted runs out of `{python} DiagnosticCounts.runs_str` still leave the failure rate as high as `{python} DiagnosticCounts.revised_fail_upper_str` at 95 percent confidence, and stopping new candidate traffic retracts no request already sent. Keep the regression tests, the bounded exposure, and the recovery owners until the outstanding effects settle.
:::

## Summary {#sec-vol3-evaluation-summary}

An agent run ends with an artifact and a report, and evaluation decides what that run is worth as evidence. The discipline throughout is to hold each claim to the evidence that supports it. A targeted pass supports its check and not the task, a trial supports its fixture and not the task population, agreement between judges supports consistency and not correctness, and a clean canary interval supports only the harms its monitor measured. Where the evidence runs out, the honest verdict is pending, unknown, or inconclusive rather than a pass. The worked comparison ends without promotion even though the candidate accepted more tasks, and that outcome is the method working as intended. A decision that names what it rests on can be revisited as evidence arrives, while a favorable scorecard cannot.

The chapter's quantitative decisions rest on the relations in @tbl-vol3-13_evaluation-key-equations, each of which either sizes the evidence a claim needs or turns that evidence into a scoped decision.

| Equation                                                                                                                                                                        | What it bounds or decides                                                                                                                             | Where derived                                        |
|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|
| $\operatorname{Var}(\hat p)=\sigma^2_{\mathrm{task}}/N+\sigma^2_{\mathrm{run}}/(NR)$                                                                                            | Whether the next evaluation budget buys new tasks or repeats; repeats stop paying once $R$ exceeds $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{run}}/\sigma^2_{\mathrm{task}}$ | @eq-variance-decomposition                           |
| $[L,U]=\tilde p\pm\frac{z}{N+z^2}\sqrt{\frac{X(N-X)}{N}+\frac{z^2}{4}}$, with $U=z^2/(N+z^2)$ at $X=0$                                                                          | The range of one acceptance or violation rate, including what a clean record of $N$ tasks still permits                                               | @eq-wilson-interval                                  |
| $\kappa=(p_o-p_e)/(1-p_e)$                                                                                                                                                      | Agreement between two raters beyond their marginal label frequencies; it measures consistency, not correctness                                        | @sec-vol3-evaluation-grading                         |
| $\hat\Delta=(c-b)/N$, variance $(\psi-\Delta^2)/N$, gate $L_\Delta>-\delta_{\mathrm{tol}}$                                                                                      | The paired acceptance difference and whether it establishes noninferiority at a declared tolerance                                                    | @sec-vol3-evaluation-paired                          |
| $N_{\text{arm}}\approx 2(z_{1-\alpha/2}+z_{1-\beta})^2\,\bar p(1-\bar p)/\Delta^2$                                                                                              | Tasks per independent arm needed to detect a difference $\Delta$ at a stated significance and power                                                   | @eq-vol3-eval-planning-power                         |
| $\operatorname{pass@}k=\mathbb{E}_i[1-(1-p_i)^k]$ and $\operatorname{pass}^k=\mathbb{E}_i[p_i^k]$                                                                               | Candidate availability in a pool of $k$ runs against consistency over $k$ recurrences of one task                                                     | @eq-pass-at-k; @eq-pass-pow-k                        |
| $C_{\text{eff,batch}}=k(g+v)/q_k$ and $C_{\text{eff,seq}}=(g+v)/p$                                                                                                              | Cost per accepted task under batch and sequential selection; the generator, not the cap, sets the sequential cost                                     | @eq-cost-per-accepted-task-iid                       |
| $(1-\theta)^{n_f}$                                                                                                                                                              | The probability that a failure mode seen $n_f$ times leaves no detailed trace under head sampling at rate $	heta$                                     | @sec-vol3-evaluation-budgets                         |
| $\Lambda_n$ against $u=\ln\frac{1-\beta}{\alpha}$ and $\ell=\ln\frac{\beta}{1-\alpha}$; $\mathbb{E}_1[N]\approx\frac{(1-\beta)u+\beta\ell}{m_1}$                                | When a canary monitor selects the degraded or the baseline hypothesis, and the labeled tasks that decision takes                                      | @eq-vol3-release-sprt; @eq-vol3-release-sprt-samples |
| $G=\mathbf{1}[L_\Delta>-\delta_{\mathrm{tol}}]\wedge\mathbf{1}[\Theta_c\ge(1-\epsilon_\Theta)\Theta_b]\wedge\mathbf{1}[\widehat T_{c,0.99}\le T_{\max}]\wedge\mathbf{1}[V_c=0]$ | Promotion: every declared criterion must hold, and nothing outside the four terms is checked                                                          | @eq-vol3-eval-release-gate                           |

: **Key equations of agent evaluation**: Each relation holds under the sampling, independence, and complete-verdict assumptions stated where it is derived; none replaces the acceptance contract or the four-verdict rule. {#tbl-vol3-13_evaluation-key-equations}

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Match every evaluation claim to its evidence"}

* **Acceptance is a contract, not a completion claim**: A trial counts only when evidence meets declared outcome, process, resource, and residual-duty criteria. Pending and unknown verdicts stay in the denominator, because dropping them changes the population and lowers the reported $C_{\text{eff}}$ without making anything cheaper.
* **A grader establishes only what it covers**: Comparable fixtures and a protected grading boundary keep a submitted artifact from shaping its own grade, yet coverage still bounds every check. Agreement between judges measures consistency; only calibration against independent assessment measures false acceptance.
* **Tasks carry the evidence; pairing multiplies it**: Repeats of one task stop adding precision once run-to-run variance is covered, so budgets buy new tasks. Running both configurations on the same tasks removes shared difficulty from the comparison, and the release question rests on that paired difference.
* **The deployment policy picks the metric**: Availability over a pool of runs suits work a checker can retry, while consistency over recurrences suits work that must succeed every time. A `{python} PassPowK.p_hi_pct_str` single-run rate passes `{python} PassPowK.k_str` recurrences only `{python} PassPowK.pow_hi_str` of the time.
* **Retention decides what diagnosis can see**: A sampler that decides before the verdict loses rare failures, and a verdict-aware sampler keeps them but biases any rate computed from what it kept. Diagnosis then tests explanations with controlled changes whose conclusions hold for their fixtures, not for the population.
* **A canary bounds only the harm it measures**: A sequential stopping rule sets the damage from a measured regression, and a smaller traffic fraction mainly stretches the time to decide. Unmeasured harms need hard tripwires, and rollback of new routing leaves outstanding effects to recovery.
* **A release is a decision record, not a scorecard**: Every declared criterion must hold, and favorable results on one cannot offset an unmet other. Claims the evidence does not support stay inconclusive, and the next experiment is planned before its data are collected.

:::

Causal and statistical release evidence (principle \ref{pri-vol3-release-evidence}) requires the decision to name its task criteria, experimental scope, and uncertainty. Recorded traces and controlled comparisons connect a finding to inspectable evidence, and the resulting gate governs a specified next step.

## Historical Perspective and Further Reading {#sec-vol3-evaluation-history}

The statistics of this chapter are older than computing. Wilson's 1927 score interval answered the problem of bounding a proportion from a small sample [@wilson1927probable], and McNemar's 1947 test answered the problem of comparing two proportions measured on the same subjects [@mcnemar1947note]. Wartime sampling inspection posed a different problem, deciding as early as the evidence allows, and Wald's sequential probability ratio test answered it [@wald1945sequential]. Agreement between human raters became measurable with Cohen's kappa [@cohen1960], and the bootstrap made uncertainty available for statistics that lack a closed form [@efron1979bootstrap]. Much later, a systematic study showed that the textbook Wald interval behaves far worse than its reputation [@brown2001interval], which is why this chapter defaults to Wilson.

Observability came from distributed systems. Lamport showed that events on separate machines admit only a partial order unless something records their causal links [@lamport1978time]. X-Trace propagated a task identifier across protocol layers and administrative domains so that one request's path could be reconstructed [@fonseca2007xtrace], and Dapper made that practical at production scale by sampling, recording spans, and keeping overhead low [@sigelman2010dapper]. Web services turned releases into experiments: online controlled experiments with ramped exposure became routine [@kohavi2008], continuous monitoring of those experiments was shown to inflate false positives without a sequential design [@johari2017peeking], and site reliability practice made the blameless postmortem a standard record [@beyer2016sre].

Machine learning evaluation followed its own path to the same lessons. Reusing a held-out set to guide decisions was shown to overfit that set, with adaptive-analysis tools to limit the damage [@dwork2015reusable], while freshly collected test sets revealed accuracy drops that their authors traced to distribution shift rather than to adaptive overfitting [@recht2019imagenet]; both effects are why this chapter separates development feedback from held-out evidence and states the task population. Code generation introduced pass@$k$ with an unbiased estimator [@chen2021evaluating], model judges were measured for their biases [@zheng2023judging], and agent benchmarks moved into interactive environments graded on resulting state [@jimenez2024swebench; @zhou2024webarena], with repeated-run consistency [@yao2024taubench] and cost-controlled comparison [@kapoor2024agents] following once single-run accuracy proved insufficient for agents.

**Further reading.**

- **Wald, "Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses"** [@wald1945sequential]: The original derivation of the sequential probability ratio test, its approximate boundaries, and its average sample number, the foundation of every staged-release monitor.
- **Brown, Cai, and DasGupta, "Interval Estimation for a Binomial Proportion"** [@brown2001interval]: A careful demonstration of why the Wald interval fails and which alternatives to use, directly relevant to small agent suites and rare violations.
- **Sigelman et al., "Dapper"** [@sigelman2010dapper]: The design of production tracing under an overhead budget, including the sampling decisions that shape what later diagnosis can see.
- **Kohavi, Tang, and Xu, *Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments*** [@kohavi2020trustworthy]: The practitioner's account of randomized comparison in live systems, from assignment units to the pitfalls that invalidate a result.
- **Dwork et al., "The Reusable Holdout"** [@dwork2015reusable]: A short paper explaining why repeatedly consulting a held-out set erodes its validity, and what a disciplined reuse protocol looks like.
- **Kapoor et al., "AI Agents That Matter"** [@kapoor2024agents]: An argument, grounded in agent benchmarks, for reporting cost alongside accuracy and for holdouts that resist overfitting.

## Exercises {#sec-vol3-13_evaluation-exercises}

Each problem states its constraints and ends in a decision about what the evidence supports or what to collect next. Givens are hypothetical unless a lighthouse profile supplies them, and every interval is a nominal 95 percent interval with $z=1.96$.

```{python}
#| label: calc-vol3-evaluation-exercises
#| echo: false
# EXERCISE GIVENS FROM THE LIGHTHOUSE PROFILES (LEGO)
# Goal: Display the remediation and support workload values the exercises use.
# Scope: Agents.Remediation.OnCall and Agents.Support.CustomerOps teaching
#        assumptions; every other exercise given is a stated hypothetical.
from mlsysim import Agents, USD
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_usd, fmt_percent, check

class EvaluationExerciseGivens:
    # 1. LOAD: lighthouse workload profiles.
    remed = Agents.Remediation.OnCall
    support = Agents.Support.CustomerOps
    impact = remed.wrong_change_impact.to(USD).magnitude  # cost when a wrong change commits
    approval = remed.approval_cost_per_attempt.to(USD).magnitude  # reviewer cost per approval
    p_support = support.acceptance_probability  # single-run acceptance of one answer
    handoff = support.handoff_cost.to(USD).magnitude  # human handoff per session

    # 2. EXECUTE: none; the exercises ask the student for every derived value.

    # 3. GUARD: the problems need an interior probability and positive costs.
    check(0 < p_support < 1, "Interior support acceptance probability")
    check(impact > approval > 0 and handoff > 0, "Positive costs; impact exceeds approval")

    # 4. OUTPUT: every export is used in the problems below.
    impact_str = fmt_usd(impact, precision=0)
    approval_str = fmt_usd(approval, precision=0)
    p_support_str = fmt_percent(p_support, precision=0, style="prose")
    handoff_str = fmt_usd(handoff, precision=0)
```

**1. New tasks or repeats (Basic).** A pilot of the repair agent's evaluation suite estimates a mean task acceptance probability of 0.6 and a between-task variance $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{task}}=0.08$. (a) Derive $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{run}}$ from these two givens using its definition in @eq-variance-decomposition, and find the number of runs per task beyond which one more repeat buys less precision than one more task. (b) With a budget of 600 graded runs, and new tasks available at no extra cost, compare the standard error of $\hat p$ for 600 tasks run once, 200 tasks run 3 times, and 100 tasks run 6 times, and choose a design. (c) Writing and validating a new hermetic fixture in fact costs as much as 10 graded runs. Within the same budget of 600 run-equivalents, find the runs per task $R$, each with the largest whole task count $N$ it affords, that minimizes $\operatorname{Var}(\hat p)$. Explain why the best design moved, and state which population the resulting estimate describes.

**2. A clean record on the replica (Basic).** The remediation agent (\ref{lhs-vol3-remediation-agent}) runs a candidate configuration on an isolated replica for 60 independently sampled incident tasks, and state-delta checks find no wrong change in any of them. From the lighthouse profile, a wrong change that commits costs `{python} EvaluationExerciseGivens.impact_str`, and the human approval that currently gates every change costs `{python} EvaluationExerciseGivens.approval_str` of reviewer time. (a) Compute the Wald and Wilson intervals for the wrong-change rate, and state which one a release record can use. (b) Ignoring any later canary check, price the Wilson upper limit as an expected loss per task and compare it with the approval cost. (c) Find how many consecutive clean replica tasks would bring that expected-loss bound below the approval cost. Decide whether the 60 clean runs justify removing human approval, and name the class of evidence that no count of replica runs can supply.

**3. Agreement is not accuracy (Basic).** Two model judges, A and B, score 200 research-agent (\ref{lhs-vol3-research-agent}) reports under the same versioned rubric. Both pass 110 reports, A passes and B fails 10, A fails and B passes 20, and both fail 60. An independent reference assessment of the same reports finds 80 failures, of which B accepted 16, and 120 passing reports, of which B accepted 114. (a) Compute the raw agreement and Cohen's $\kappa$ between the judges. (b) Compute B's false-acceptance rate $P(\mathrm{Acc}\mid F)$ with its Wilson interval, and the failure fraction among B's acceptances, $P(F\mid\mathrm{Acc})$. (c) The release policy admits a judge as an acceptance grader only if the Wilson upper limit on its false-acceptance rate is at most 10 percent. Decide whether B qualifies, and state what a random audit of B-accepted reports alone could and could not establish.

**4. Paired evidence for the offline gate (Intermediate).** A repair-agent comparison runs one baseline and one candidate trial on each of 200 independently sampled tasks, with complete verdicts: both accepted on 120 tasks, only the baseline on $b=6$, only the candidate on $c=16$, and neither on 58. The declared tolerance is $\delta_{\mathrm{tol}}=2$ percentage points. (a) Compute $\hat\Delta$, the discordant fraction $\psi$, and a normal-approximation paired interval from the variance $(\psi-\Delta^2)/N$. Decide whether the candidate is noninferior and whether it is superior. (b) Compute each configuration's separate Wilson interval, and show what a team that required non-overlapping intervals would have decided. (c) Compute the ratio of independent-arm variance to paired variance at these acceptance rates, and the number of tasks per independent arm that would match the paired precision. (d) Compute the exact two-sided McNemar value. Explain how it can sit just above 0.05 while the paired interval excludes zero, and state which result the declared gate uses.

**5. Choose the generator, not the cap (Intermediate).** The repair agent selects sequentially, stopping at the first candidate that passes an exact checker costing $v=\$0.04$ per candidate. Generator A passes with $p=0.3$ at $g=\$0.05$ per candidate; generator B passes with $p=0.5$ at $g=\$0.12$. (a) Compute $C_{\text{eff,seq}}$ for each generator. (b) The task deadline allows at most 4 sequential candidates, and the contract requires availability $q_k\ge 0.90$ within that cap. Determine which generator meets it, and the smallest cap generator A would need. (c) A teammate proposes generator A with all candidates generated and checked in parallel at the cap from (b) so that the deadline holds. Compute $C_{\text{eff,batch}}$ for that design and compare it with generator B under sequential selection. (d) The team replaces the checker with the full regression suite at $v=\$0.20$. Recompute both sequential costs, find the checking cost at which the two generators tie, and state the design rule the crossover illustrates.

**6. Second lighthouse: the support agent's consistency (Intermediate).** The support agent (\ref{lhs-vol3-support-agent}) answers a refund-policy question correctly on `{python} EvaluationExerciseGivens.p_support_str` of single runs, and the same customer asks it in 5 separate sessions. A wrong answer that a customer has read cannot be retried, and a human handoff costs `{python} EvaluationExerciseGivens.handoff_str` per session. (a) Compute pass$^k$ over the 5 sessions, the single-run rate that would hold 90 percent consistency, and the factor by which the single-run failure rate must fall. For contrast, compute pass@$3$ at the same single-run rate, the quantity a repair agent with a checker in the loop could use. (b) A policy-grounded model judge now screens each answer before delivery, with $\epsilon_{\text{FA}}=0.20$ and $\epsilon_{\text{FR}}=0.05$, and every rejected answer goes to a human handoff. Per session, compute the probability that a wrong answer reaches the customer, the handoff probability, and the expected handoff cost; then compute the probability that all 5 sessions deliver no wrong answer. (c) Find the largest $\epsilon_{\text{FA}}$ that holds 90 percent over the 5 sessions, and the expected handoff cost per session at that rate. (d) Contrast the constraint that binds this agent's evaluation claim with the one that binds the repair agent's, and state which grader measurement the support agent's release record must therefore carry.

**7. A retention budget for rare failures (Intermediate).** A repair fleet runs 20,000 evaluation trials per day, each with a 2 MB (decimal) permitted trace body. At the selection boundary, 3 percent of trials have failed a criterion, 1 percent remain pending or unknown, and the rest are ordinary accepted trials. One failure mode occurs 8 times per week, and downstream diagnostic storage is capped at 1.5 GB per day. (a) Compute the daily volume of full retention and of uniform head sampling at $\theta=2$ percent, and the probability that head sampling keeps no detailed trace of the rare mode in a week. (b) Compute the daily volume of tail selection that keeps every failed and unresolved trial plus a 1 percent random control sample of ordinary trials, and check it against the cap. (c) Design a selection policy within the cap that keeps every failed trial. State the sampling rates for unresolved and ordinary trials, the inclusion probabilities the record must keep, and one change to the trace body that would relax the cap. (d) An analyst reports the fraction of retained traces under the policy of part (b) that failed as the fleet's failure rate. Compute the reported value, and name the record the failure rate must come from.

**8. Size a canary against a deadline (Advanced).** A repair-agent canary monitors acceptance with the SPRT of @eq-vol3-release-sprt, comparing $p_0=0.80$ with $p_1=0.70$ at design targets $\alpha=0.05$ and $\beta=0.10$. Eligible tasks arrive regularly at 40 per hour, each label arrives 2 hours after admission when the regression suite finishes, and under $p_1$ the monitor must decide within 24 hours of the first admission. Separately, a harm the monitor does not measure occurs in 0.5 percent of candidate tasks, and release policy requires the candidate to run for 7 days at its allocation before any wider release. (a) Compute $u$, $\ell$, $m_1$, and the no-overshoot $\mathbb{E}_1[N]$. (b) Find the smallest allocation $\rho$ that meets the decision deadline. (c) Compute the expected excess failures from the measured regression at that $\rho$ and at $\rho=25$ percent. (d) Compute the expected count of unmeasured harms over the 7-day period at both allocations. Choose $\rho$ and justify it from parts (b) through (d). (e) A teammate proposes replacing the SPRT with a fixed-sample test rerun after every new label, stopping at the first value below 0.05. Critique the proposal.

**9. Critique a release report (Advanced).** A team asks to promote a repair-agent candidate with the following evidence. The candidate accepted 78 percent of tasks and the baseline 72 percent, reported as a 6-point gain. The baseline ran on 100 tasks sampled last month, and the candidate on 100 newly sampled tasks. The team dropped 12 candidate trials whose regression suites had not finished, so the candidate accepted 69 of the remaining 88. Report quality counted as accepted when an LLM judge scored it at least 4 of 5, justified by 90 percent raw agreement with a second judge. The failure rate in the release notes was computed from tail-sampled traces. (a) Under the four-verdict rule, bound the candidate's accepted fraction of its admitted cohort, and state what the 6-point claim becomes. (b) Using @eq-vol3-eval-planning-power with $\bar p=0.75$, a 5 percent two-sided significance target, and 80 percent power, compute the tasks per independent arm needed to detect a 6-point difference. (c) Redesign the comparison as paired. Assuming a discordant fraction $\psi=0.15$, an anticipated gain of 3 points, and $\delta_{\mathrm{tol}}=2$ points, find the number of task pairs at which the normal-approximation lower limit $\hat\Delta-z\sqrt{(\psi-\hat\Delta^2)/N}$ clears $-\delta_{\mathrm{tol}}$ if the gain holds. (d) Identify the remaining defects in the report and write a defensible protocol: which criteria the automated gate enforces, which measurements the judge must carry, and which conditions the team must declare before collecting data.

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From evaluation evidence to curated trajectories"}

Which of these trajectories should become training data, and which failures call for a change outside the model? @Sec-vol3-trajectory-curation uses evaluation evidence to guide diagnosis, admission, and corpus design. A logged success is not automatically a useful demonstration, and a failure is not automatically a policy defect. Preserve criterion and configuration provenance, unresolved evidence, and the separation between development data and held-out evaluation. Curation turns that qualified record into a learning-data decision.

:::
